title: Artin–Schreier on algebraically closed fields
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic
$p>0$. Then the Artin–Schreier map

$$
\wp:k\longrightarrow k,\qquad \wp(x)=x^p-x,
$$

is surjective, with kernel $\mathbf F_p$.

proof.text: Since $k$ has characteristic $p>0$ [def-pc-field-characteristic], $p\ge2$ (no field has $1_k=0$). Given $a\in k$, the polynomial $X^p-X-a\in k[X]$ has degree $p\ge2$, so it is nonconstant and, $k$ being algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure], has a root $x\in k$; then $x^p-x=a$. Hence $\wp$ is surjective.

Since $k$ is a field of characteristic $p>0$ [def-pc-field-characteristic], $p$ is prime (a factorization $p=mn$ with $1<m,n<p$ would give $(m\cdot1_k)(n\cdot1_k)=0$ with both factors nonzero), and $p\cdot1_k=0$. The kernel condition $x^p-x=0$ is equivalent to $x^p=x$. The field Artin–Schreier kernel node [lem-sc-field-artin-schreier-kernel], applied to $K=k$, identifies exactly these elements with the image of the canonical $\mathbf F_p=\mathbf Z/p\mathbf Z$ in $k$ (the prime subfield), which is the stated kernel $\mathbf F_p$.
